newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Nov 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Nov 11.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on November 11. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Guruh Sukarnoputra, Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) legislator and brother of ousted PDI leader Megawati Sukarnoputri, has caused a stir by attending anniversary celebrations of a group aligned to the ruling Golkar party.
The government has ruled that all new industrial plants in the outskirts of Jakarta in Bogor, Tengerang, Bekasi and Karawang in West Java must be established in industrial estates.
President Suharto told the Indonesian Communion of Churches that he is worried about the use of violence in resolving conflict, especially religious conflict.

Members of Indonesia's parliament said they appreciated the actions of the Malaysian youths who broke into a conference on East Timor in Kuala Lumpur on Saturday causing the meeting to be abandoned after police had intervened to restore order.

A consortium formed by President Suharto's son Bambang Trihatmodjo has proposed that all government offices be moved to a new office complex in a special zone to the southeast of the Jakarta metropolitan area near the hill town of Bogor being designed by the consortium.
